newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia looks to boost trade with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Australia looks to boost trade with Iraq.

text.p: Australia is confident of boosting exports to Iraq after sending its first trade mission to Baghdad since the 1991 Gulf War, officials said on Monday.

"We believe that some real progress was made for the development of Australian exports to Iraq within the framework of (international) sanctions," foreign affairs department spokesman Nick Warner told reporters.
A trade delegation which included business executives visited Baghdad from May 4 to 7 as part of Canberra's efforts to rebuild Australia's commercial profile.
Warner said the mission found there were particular opportunities to sell commodities, pharmaceutical products, herbicides and pumps to Iraq.
The United Nations Security Council imposed sanctions, including a ban on regular Iraqi oil sales, soon after Iraq invaded neighbouring Kuwait in August 1990.
Last December, it enacted a special arrangement allowing Baghdad to sell US$2.0 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine to help ease conditions for its people.
Australia recently struck a substantial deal to sell wheat to Iraq under the oil-for-food programme. Before the Gulf War, Iraq took about one million tonnes of Australian wheat a year.
Australian trade with Iraq has been negligible for several years due to the sanctions.
